text:
eli: quick brain-dump: proposal to add a "deadline-fence" header + a tiny "fallback-marker" stream trailer so clients can detect midstream graceful downgrades and show appropriate UI instead of a surprise timeout. want to capture tradeoffs + rollout plan.
maria: sounds promising. what does "deadline-fence" buy us vs just honoring client deadlines?
eli: fence tells gateway a hard SLO boundary for that call (e.g., 800ms). gateway can use it to stop hedging into slow paths and instead attempt cheaper fallbacks once fence crosses. also useful for telemetry: mark when gateway violated fence.
dom: +1 but two concerns: 1) how do we avoid leaking server timing info? 2) how to treat retries and idempotency?
noah: for privacy: default fence is not echoed to downstream unless client opts in. we can make header explicit: `X-RW-Deadline-Fence: 800ms; opt_in=true|false`. opt_in=true means gateway may emit `fallback-marker` events with reasons.
maria: explain fallback-marker wire-format? trailers vs inline events?
eli: minimal: NDJSON trailing events (very small) after partial tokens or at finalization. example line: `{"marker_id":"f-123","stage":"fallback","reason":"latency_threshold","variant":"light-encoder"}`. Keep it opt-in. Clients can then correlate marker_id with a lease/token to display "showing faster condensed answer".
dom: how does this interact with prefix caching? If cache serves quick partial, we should emit `stage=cache-final` so UI stops spinner. But careful: cache might have stale or redacted content; add `source=cache` flag and restrict variant info.
noah: retries: progress_id + attempt suffix pattern works well: `f-123-1`, `f-123-2`. Gateway increments attempt when it routes to fallback. That way SDK can show "attempting fallback (2)".
maria: admission policy sketch: gateway keeps reserved "fast-lane" tokens for fence-bound calls. Admission score = base - penalty(priority) - (time_in_queue / fence). If time_in_queue > fence * 0.6, consider fallback. Also set a min_time_to_first_token threshold before preempting.
dom: eviction rules: don't evict calls that are past first_token or marked `progress_nonpreemptable`. For low-priority, mark as preemptable until `first_token`. Also, define a cap: high-priority reserve N% (configurable).
observability-bot: suggestion: add span tags `fence.ms`, `fallback.marker_id`, `fallback.reason`, `fallback.attempt`. metrics: `fence.violations_count`, `fallback.emitted_rate`, `time_to_fallback.p95`.
eli: privacy note: restrict `variant` field unless route-level permission. Better to emit coarse reasons only (`latency`, `memory`, `capacity`).
oah: SDKs: map fence -> UI thresholds. If client sets fence=800ms, SDK shows succinct summary after fallback-marker stage; otherwise keep spinner. We'll ship a tiny SDK util to parse marker and attempt suffix.
maria: operational plan: 1) implement header parsing and opt-in gating in gateway behind ff `deadline-fence-v1`; 2) implement sparse trailer NDJSON emission (on stage-change or final) in gateway; 3) SDK util + README; 4) observability tags + alert `p95 time_to_fallback > 1.2 * fence` for fence-bound routes.
dom: rollout: prototype on a single non-critical route (assistant-snippets), sample 5% traffic. Measure noise and metric cardinality for 2 weeks. Tune reserved fast-lane % and eviction thresholds.
eli: sample trailer payload we plan to emit (string): `{"marker_id":"f-123-1","stage":"cache-final","reason":"cache_hit","attempt":1}`. Keep it tiny and human-readable.
noah: for retries we should keep attempt cap (e.g., max 3) and make SDKs disable opt-in automatically after repeated fallbacks to avoid flapping UIs.
maria: compatibility: if client doesn't opt-in, gateway is opaque (no trailers). Server-side default no-variant info. Private deployments must enable feature explicitly.
observability-bot: recommended alert: `increase in fence.violations_count post-deploy` and `fallback.emitted_rate spike` correlated to rollout. Add sampling flag to trailer emission to control cardinality.
eli: owners: @eli proto in gateway, @noah SDK util + README, @maria observability + RFC follow-up, @dom eviction math. I'll open PR with minimal header parsing and a flag to enable NDJSON trailers.
maria: thanks. quick nit: pick safe defaults: fence opt_in=false, reserved_fast_lane=12%, attempt_cap=3, trailer_sampling=0.2. We'll iterate.
noah: I'll draft SDK examples showing UX mapping for fence values (500ms, 800ms, 1500ms).
eli: ok filing RFC follow-up now. ping when staging PR lands. :thumbsup:
